newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures drifted lower on Monday in a lacklustre session marked by a negative reaction to stronger-than-expected U.S. economic releases the day before the Federal Reserve's policy setting council meets.

Traders said the contract began to head south after failing to break through resistance at 129.52/54 after several tests early in the day, trailing the Bund market lower, but remained above key technical support at 129.06.
September PIBOR also struggled to break through resistance at 96.61-63 despite the strength of the franc and was hit late in the session by non-resident fund sales, traders said.

Traders said a report from Germany's Ifo economic research institute saying central banks may be forced to implement more restrictive monetary policy to stabilise exchange rates dented sentiment initially.

Then a stronger-than-expected rise in a June Chicago purchasing managers index dented prices further in European and U.S. bond markets, especially given the caution ahead of the Fed's policy setting meeting.
Analysts said even if the U.S. central bank left interest rates unchanged, as most expected, concerns the economy could rebound later in the year might dampen the positive impact.

Guy Stear, bond analyst at Societe Generale, said although French bonds had resisted the declines in the U.S. market last week, further declines in Treasuries and Bunds could push them below their recent range.

French 10-year bonds outperformed their German counterparts on Monday, the yield spread moved to minus 13 from minus 12 on Friday, and analysts said a 30-year Bund issue this week could weigh on the German long end.
French 30-year bonds also outperformed and the spread moved to parity from plus one last week.

A growing belief that U.S. interest rates would be raised in the coming months boosted the dollar against European currencies. The French franc fell to 5.8915, its lowest level since April 1994, but climbed against the mark to 3.3695, its highest level since June 2.
Traders said PIBOR failed to benefit from the franc strength against the mark as profit taking by non-resident investors weighed on the contract late in the session.
The September contract peaked at 96.61 resistance before slipping to 96.55 after one fund sold 5,000 lots at 96.57-58, traders said.
